purpose: Transparent model behind the chat-versus-video comparison. Every input carries claim ids from footprint.json (fp-), demand.json (dem-) or tradeoffs.json (tr-) and a basis label: measured (a meter or operator production data), reported (a company or survey total), or modeled (an estimate, allocation or this file's arithmetic). The page script reproduces these equations and checks its totals against computed_defaults. Ranges are low and high inputs run through the same equations, not confidence intervals.

chat_wh_per_prompt.basis: measured (Google production median 0.24) and modeled (Joule median 0.31, interquartile 0.16 to 0.60; Jegham GPT-4o short prompt 0.42; OpenAI statement 0.34 'average query', no method; Epoch 0.6 including a development share)
chat_wh_per_prompt.note: Text prompts only. 0.24 and 0.31 are medians: Google reports the median because the per-prompt distribution is skewed and the arithmetic mean is pulled up by a few heavy prompts, so any count times 0.30 is a floor. mean (0.34) is the only average-class figure in the record and carries no boundary; sums are also run at it. Reasoning, long-context, image, video and agent work are in heavy_ai and in the chat_kind setting.

chat_kb_per_prompt.basis: modeled from one phone-app measurement (several KB per prompt, 62 KB for a web-search prompt); 500 KB is an allowance for web clients and images

video_dc_wh_per_gb.basis: modeled from measured hours: DIMPACT participants' 1.3 Wh per streaming hour (fp-122) over Carbon Trust's 2.88 GB average hour (fp-130) gives 0.45; Carbon Trust's own 1 Wh hour (fp-037) gives 0.35. The low is the DESNZ follow-up of 07/28/2026, 0.6 Wh per viewing hour (fp-141), or 0.171 Wh per GB by our division (fp-142). The high is Sustainable Web Design's top-down 55 Wh per GB (ec-024, fp-147), all data center energy over all internet bytes. One operator measured 1.15 (sv-048)
video_dc_wh_per_gb.note: The spread is an unsettled allocation, not a measurement error (fp-149). The DESNZ first report's 19.6 Wh per GB is retired by its authors (fp-144), so it is no longer a reading here. The high end cannot be a literal per-hour share: at 3.5 GB an hour it is above whole-chain figures (fp-150), so it is shown only as an upper bound. Every video row is GB times this intensity; the reader-chosen setting is video_dc_intensity.

short_dc_ceiling_wh_per_hour.unit: Wh per hour of short-video feed, ceiling
short_dc_ceiling_wh_per_hour.basis: modeled bound: Meta's 15.1 Wh per daily active person per day spread over 65 minutes of daily Facebook and Instagram use (ENGIE) gives 13.9 Wh per hour; over Similarweb's 100 Instagram minutes, 9.1. All Meta products, AI training and offices included
short_dc_ceiling_wh_per_hour.note: The short row's data center segment is short_gb_per_hour times video_dc_wh_per_gb (delivery only; ranking and recommendation compute are unmeasured), capped at this ceiling per hour and at 15.1 Wh per day. No source measures the data center side of an Instagram or TikTok hour. ENGIE excludes Meta's data centers (fp-051).

meta_wh_per_person_day.unit: Wh per daily active person per day
meta_wh_per_person_day.basis: reported (Meta 2024: 18.42 TWh total electricity over 3.35 billion daily active people)
meta_wh_per_person_day.note: A company-wide fleet average per daily active person that counts AI training, ads, Reality Labs and offices. Not a bound on any one feed (a heavy Instagram user sits above a fleet average that includes WhatsApp-only people) and not on the chat row's text-inference boundary.

net_mobile_avg_wh_per_gb.basis: modeled (DESNZ 2024 extrapolation 25; Carbon Trust 2020 100; ENGIE Europe 2022 top-down 183)

net_fixed_marginal_wh_per_gb.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust power model: dynamic part of core and access power for a 6.67 Mbps stream)

net_mobile_marginal_wh_per_gb.basis: modeled (ENGIE short-term marginal 8.6 mWh per 2.5 MB; Carbon Trust power model agrees)

router_watts.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust 10 W router; DIMPACT 9 to 15 W); measured 5.88 Wh per hour for a home router during 1080p phone streaming (TNO poster)
router_watts.note: A shared always-on device: by_time charges its whole hourly draw to one person's activity, the same for every row, so it never explains a difference between rows and is shown as a separate fixed band.

router_wh_per_gb.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust conventional allocation of a 10 W router by household data)

phone.basis: measured for video (TNO 2.22 at 75 percent brightness; Greenspector YouTube 5.28 mAh per minute, about 1.2 Wh per hour at 3.85 V and 50 percent brightness); modeled for chat (Greenspector ChatGPT 5.5 to 7.2 mAh per minute, 1.05 to 1.36 times its YouTube rate); DIMPACT 1 to 2 W
phone.note: Battery energy, not wall energy; charging losses would add roughly a third (EPA 19 Wh per charge, fp-073).

laptop.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust Table 10 portable computer 22 W; DIMPACT 15 to 30 W)

tv.basis: modeled (100 W television in Google, DIMPACT, DESNZ and Carbon Trust; DIMPACT range 40 to 120 W)

phone.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust: SD 1, HD 3, mobile save-data 0.17, automatic 0.25)

laptop.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust laptop mix 55 percent SD, 45 percent HD)

mix.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust European device mix, 70 percent television); used only to turn the measured per-hour data center figures into Wh per GB and for the YouTube total

short_gb_per_hour.basis: modeled (ENGIE 256 MB per day over 39.5 minutes of 700 kb/s video; upper allowance for HD feeds and preloading)

chat_messages_per_day.basis: reported mean per weekly user per day, counting days of non-use (OpenAI: 18 billion messages a week over 700 million weekly users; fp-092 calls it a mean over light and heavy users, not a typical person); a per-active-day figure is unpublished and would be higher; 8 is Jegham's high case, which the Reuters item it cites does not contain (fp-094, unverified)
chat_messages_per_day.panel_note: Epoch AI's opted-in US panel (fp-154), a selected group with survivorship bias; a reference beside OpenAI's mean, not a replacement for it.

short_minutes_per_day.basis: reported (Similarweb, Instagram 100 and TikTok 115 minutes, August 2026)

household_wh_per_day.basis: reported (EIA 2025 residential average, 10,491 kWh per year)

stream_whole_chain_wh_per_hour.unit: Wh per streaming hour, data center plus network plus router plus device
stream_whole_chain_wh_per_hour.basis: modeled published hours: Carbon Trust 2020 Europe 188 (70 percent television, router by data); Preist 2016 YouTube 53.7 (no idle equipment, low bitrate); BBC 2024 UK 65.7 (no standby); DESNZ follow-up 2026 scenario 118.7, 192.3 and 263.1 (low, medium, high), which replaced its first report's 162.5 to 417.5. The low and high are the sources' own extremes, not the span of central estimates
stream_whole_chain_wh_per_hour.note: Used only as the published yardstick in view 3 and for the YouTube total in view 4; view 1 builds its own hour from segments and view 3 also uses that hour.

OpenAI o3, long prompt (10k in, 1.5k out)
DeepSeek-R1 on its own servers, long prompt
heavy_ai.basis: modeled (Jegham; low is the same model on Azure)

heavy_ai.label: One 1024 x 1024 image, Stable Diffusion 3 Medium
heavy_ai.basis: measured GPU energy 0.317, doubled for overhead (MIT Technology Review assumption)

heavy_ai.label: One image, open models of 2023 (Luccioni)
heavy_ai.basis: measured on one node, no PUE

heavy_ai.label: Sora 2 Pro, 8-second clip (estimate, same paper)
heavy_ai.basis: modeled (scaling laws, preprint; claim fp-137; value is the paper's own mean)

heavy_ai.label: Wan2.1 1.3B open model, 5-second 720p clip
heavy_ai.basis: measured on one H100, no PUE

heavy_ai.label: Wan2.1 14B open model, 5-second 720p clip
heavy_ai.basis: measured on one H100, no PUE

heavy_ai.label: Claude Code, one typed prompt (one heavy user)
Claude Code, median session (one heavy user)
Claude Code, average day (one heavy user)

chatgpt_messages_per_day.unit: messages per day, July 2025, consumer plans
chatgpt_messages_per_day.note: One product; Gemini, Claude, Copilot and API traffic are not counted, so the chat total is a floor.

youtube_hours_per_day.basis: reported for 2016 (as used by Preist et al.); a floor for today

nw_dc_only_2030_amw.basis: modeled (NW Council workbook, data centers without chip fabs)

nw_dc_share_of_growth_pct.basis: modeled (NW Council draft Ninth Plan futures, 2025 to 2046)

lbnl_site_wue_l_per_kwh.basis: modeled (2023 plateau; range is the post-2023 scenario)

lbnl_indirect_water_l_per_kwh.basis: modeled (US data center grid mix, 2023; all-sector 4.35)

li_gpt3_response_water_ml.basis: modeled, GPT-3 era, on-site plus generation

us_grid_average_g_per_kwh.basis: reported (US average May 2024 to April 2025); hyperscale-weighted 545

epa_marginal_lb_per_mwh.basis: reported (EPA equivalencies calculator non-baseload rate, 2022); equals about 637 g per kWh

streaming_gco2e_per_hour.basis: modeled (Carbon Trust 2020 Europe 56; BBC 2024 UK 14.8; IEA 2019 36)

instagram_gco2e_per_min.basis: modeled (Greenspector, France, phone plus projected server share)

comparators.label: One hour of a 60 W-equivalent LED bulb
One hour of a 100 W television
One mile in a typical passenger car (carbon only)
IEA: a simple text query uses less electricity than running a television for the same time
One minute of an 800 W microwave
comparators.source_kind: none in the record: DOE's microwave standard regulates standby power only; 800 W is the Carbon Trust and MIT Technology Review convention
comparators.note: Not for a chart until an agency wattage is found.

prompts_per_hour.label: Prompts the reader sends in the hour
prompts_per_hour.why: No source measures a chat hour. Epoch AI's panel has a median of 2 prompts per conversation (fp-151) and 4.3 prompts a day (fp-154), with no duration; WildChat's older free-service mean is 2.52 per conversation (fp-095); OpenAI users average 3.67 per day (fp-034). Ten per hour is one every six minutes, slow for someone chatting steadily, so 2.52, 10, 30 and 60 are offered as equal presets; 30 and 60 are heavy-use sensitivities with no field support, and no preset is the answer.

connection.label: Connection
connection.why: Cellular uses the mobile intensity and has no home router.

network_mode.label: Network accounting
network_mode.why: Average divides a network's whole energy by its traffic; marginal counts only the extra energy one more stream causes. Published figures differ by 10 to 50 times (fp-053, fp-129).

router_allocation.label: Home router
router_allocation.why: by_time charges the router's 10 W to every hour it is used (same for every app); by_data follows the Carbon Trust convention (25 Wh per GB); excluded follows BBC, which leaves always-on equipment out.

video_dc_intensity.label: Streaming data center energy per GB served
video_dc_intensity.why: measured_delivery is DIMPACT participants' 1.3 Wh per streaming hour over Carbon Trust's 2.88 GB average hour (fp-122, fp-130). desnz_followup is the DESNZ follow-up study of 07/28/2026: 0.6 Wh per viewing hour (fp-141), or 0.171 Wh per GB by our division (fp-142). It replaced the first report's 19.6 Wh per GB, which its authors retired after clarifying what the figure counted (fp-144). top_down is Sustainable Web Design's 55 Wh per GB, all data center energy over all internet bytes (ec-024, fp-147), an upper bound and not a literal share (fp-150). The allocation is unsettled (fp-149).

chat_wh_per_prompt.label: Energy per text prompt in the data center
chat_wh_per_prompt.why: The text slider; chat_kind overrides it for other kinds of chat.

chat_kind.label: Kind of chat (sets the energy per prompt)
chat_kind.why: The text slider stops at 0.60, below GPT-5 minimal reasoning (0.67), Claude 3.7 (0.95) and o3 (1.18) in the same preprint. medium_prompt is Jegham's GPT-4o medium query (fp-021); reasoning is Joule's query 15 times longer than typical (fp-019); high_reasoning is Jegham's GPT-5 high reasoning, medium query (fp-025). Jegham is a preprint that Joule says overstates production figures by 4 to 20 times (fp-020). A multi-turn chat carries growing context and agents make about 12 model calls per typed prompt (fp-031); no source counts model calls per chat prompt.

chat_messages_per_day.label: Prompts per day for the per-person view

battery_nominal_volts.label: Lithium-ion nominal voltage used to turn Greenspector mAh rates into Wh
battery_nominal_volts.why: Plain assumption; typical phone battery nominal voltage. Not a claim.

same_hour.title: The same hour on the same device

equations.chat.network: prompts_per_hour x chat_kb_per_prompt / 1e6 GB x net intensity (fixed or mobile; average or marginal)
equations.video.data_center: video_gb_per_hour[device] x video_dc_intensity (measured_delivery 0.45, desnz_followup 0.171, or top_down 55 Wh per GB)
equations.*.router: by_time: router_watts x 1 h; by_data: router_wh_per_gb x row GB (wifi only); excluded: 0; cellular: 0
equations.*.device: device_wh_per_hour[device] x 1 h (same for every row)
equations.*.activity_added: data_center + network: the segments that depend on what the hour is spent on; router and device are a fixed band, identical on every row

per_person_day.title: Inside the data center only, per person per day

equations.chat_day: chat_messages_per_day x chat_wh_per_prompt (a median times a mean count: a floor; chat_day_mean uses the 0.34 average-class figure; low is the low count times the low prompt)
equations.meta_person: meta_wh_per_person_day (a fleet average on another boundary and another denominator; printed, not compared as a ratio)
equations.video_day: video_minutes_per_day / 60 x video_gb_per_hour[phone] x video_dc_intensity (Similarweb minutes are Android app minutes)
equations.short_day: short_minutes_per_day / 60 x short_gb_per_hour x video_dc_intensity; high case min(minutes / 60 x short_dc_ceiling_wh_per_hour, 15.1)

heavy_ai.title: Heavy AI against the same yardstick

equations.stream_hours_same_device: Wh / view 1 video total for the reader's device
equations.stream_hours_dc_only: Wh / view 1 video data center segment for the reader's device (measured_delivery; desnz_followup printed beside it)

heavy_ai.note: The AI side is data center only. The same-device and published hours include the viewer's screen and router, so those ratios flatter AI; the data-center-only ratio is like for like but rests on the 45-times serving-intensity dispute. All are printed; none is the answer.

equations.chat_twh_per_year: chatgpt_messages_per_day x 365 x chat_wh_per_prompt / 1e12 (text-only floor, median prompt, July 2025 count; also run at the 0.34 mean)
equations.youtube_dc_twh_per_year: youtube_hours_per_day x 365 x video_gb_per_hour[mix] x video_dc_intensity / 1e12
equations.withdrawn: chat share of the 2030 Pacific Northwest data center load: a 07/2025 count of one product's text messages against a 2030 workbook input; deleted after review

project.title: A proposed project (the reader enters MW and load factor)

equations.share_of_region: aMW / nw_region_amw (22,000, the Council region: Oregon, Idaho, Washington and Western Montana)
equations.site_water_liters_per_year: TWh x 1e9 kWh x the applicant's stated L per kWh; record spread on a consumption basis: Microsoft 0.27, LBNL 0.36 rising to 0.45 to 0.48 after 2023, Google 1.15; Meta's 0.19 is withdrawal and not on the same bar

project.note: This comparison does not decide a proposal. It says nothing about a site, a stream, a rate class, or Treaty-reserved rights; those are the Questions for Tribal Leaders on the data centers page (Consent, Land, Water, Power, Rates, Jobs, Data, Exit Terms), and reserved-rights items are for counsel. A fleet average cannot describe a stream in a low-flow August.
